previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis, depression, and a history of C. difficile infection, was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back. She was found to have a recurrence of Clostridium difficile colitis, confirmed by a positive stool PCR test. She was treated with IV metronidazole and oral vancomycin, along with IV fluids and her established pain and nausea protocol including Dilaudid, promethazine, and lorazepam. A right PICC line was placed for reliable access. Her symptoms improved, she transitioned to oral intake, and her labs stabilized. Blood pressure was managed with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. She was discharged home on a full course of vancomycin, with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and continue all home medications including Creon, amitriptyline, and quetiapine.

#) ABDOMINAL PAIN/NAUSEA: Likely a flare up of chronic 
pancreatitis.  Excluded C.diff with negative PCR.  The patient 
was treated per her established inpatient protocol (from ___ 
as below.  IV access was difficult to obtain but ultimately a 
midline was obtained by the ___ RN in the left AC.  The patient 
was pleasant and cooperative and did not ask for additional 
narcotics other than those outlined in her protocol.  By 
hospital day 3, she was tolerating PO, asked to be switched to 
PO medications which she tolerated, and then ultimately was 
weaned entirely from narcotics and was discharged without any 
prescriptions for controlled substances.
- IVF @ 100cc/hr
- Dilaudid 2 mg IV Q3hrs PRN pain in 50cc NS over 15 minutes
- Toradol 30 mg IV/IM Q8hrs for three days
- Promethazine 25 mg IV Q6hrs PRN nausea
- Lorazepam 1mg Q ___ IV PRN anxiety/nausea
- Lorazepam 1 mg qhs IV PRN insomnia (in addition to above 
Ativan
if needed)  **this was changed to 2mg as an outpatient, and 
reflected in her intpatient order set**
- When can tolerate PO -> 4mg dilaudid q3h:prn

#) TOXICOLOGY SCREEN: Patient positive for opiates in urine in 
ED 1 hour after receiving IV hydromorphone.  This is likely too 
fast to be detected in the urine and is a synthetic opiate.  
Barbiturate positive screen likely from fioricet.  This 
information was passed to her PCP.

#) HYPERTENSION: Held HCTZ due to hypovolemia.  Blood pressure 
was subsequently poorly controlled and she was started 
lisinopril and continued at discharge.

#) DEPRESSION: Stable mood with no SI/HI.  Continued 
amitriptyline
#) ANXIETY: Well controlled.  Continued lorazepam and quetiapine
#) CHRONIC PAIN: Continued tramadol when tolerated PO
